2011_030_120611regmtg.paragraph: The Troy School District Board of Education packet for the regular meeting of Tuesday, December 6, 2011, 7:00 p.m. at the Services Building, 4420 Livernois, pairs the October 2011 Treasurer's Report and a full October check register with reports on full-day kindergarten, the Summer Success Academy, and the Facilities Study, plus MESSA and policyholder resolutions. The check register totals $3,318,441.42 across all funds, and total disbursements in the period are reported as $6,307,840.15. The Business item asks the Board to certify compliance with at least four of five criteria under Section 22f of the State School Aid Act to claim the $100 per pupil Best Practices incentive.

**Meeting**
Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting, Tuesday, December 6, 2011, 7:00 p.m., Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098; district offices 4400 Livernois, 248.823.4000, www.troy.k12.mi.us. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 58 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW).

**Recognition**
Troy High physics teacher John Morrison and physics club students won Lemelson-MIT InvenTeam status for a mechanical-assist stair climber, one of 15 high school teams nationally, with a $10,000 prototype award and a June showcase at EurekaFest on the MIT campus in Cambridge, Massachusetts.

**Consent agenda**
November 1, 2011 minutes; November 15, 2011 workshop minutes; October 2011 Treasurer's Report. The November 1 meeting (7:00 p.m.–8:48 p.m., President Philippart presiding) passed Resolution 11-098 (consent), 11-099 (new hire Melissa Marsack) and 11-100 accepting the audited 2011 financial statements presented by Plante & Moran's Teresa Pollock with an unqualified opinion — each 7 ayes, 0 nays. Recognitions included Heather Kelly (ArtPrize 2011, "Wish Project"), Rebecca Brewer (2011 ING Unsung Heroes, $27,000 for "Mini-Med School – Simulating Surgeries"), the HealthierUS School Challenge Bronze Award (banner, plaque and $500 to each of 12 elementary schools), and Robert Stromayer's 23 years at Niles Continuing Education.

Largest checks: MESSA $996,933.25; Hewlett Packard $841,010.00 (2004 Capital Project Fund); Enviro Clean Services $248,236.57; Merit Network $148,865.23; First Group America $100,414.70 (special education transportation) and $91,483.52 (general education).

**Action and report items**
Personnel: execution of the MESSA Employer Participation Agreement and a Policyholder Resolution under Section 22f(1), 2011 PA 62 (MCL 388.1622f(1)). Business: Best Practices resolution certifying four of five criteria for the $100 per pupil incentive by June 1, 2012. Curriculum: full-day kindergarten for 2012-2013 with a draft implementation timeline, and the Summer Success Academy report (49 students). Other: Facilities Study update from co-chairs Greg Bryen and Waqar Hashim, recommendations due February 7, 2012; approval for Board President Philippart to attend the NSBA Federal Relations Network Conference in Washington, D.C., February 5–7, 2012; closed session on negotiations under the Open Meetings Act.

**Identification.** Board packet for the Troy School District Board of Education regular meeting of Tuesday, December 6, 2011, 7:00 p.m., Services Building, 4420 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098; the masthead gives 4400 Livernois, Troy, Michigan 48098, 248.823.4000, www.troy.k12.mi.us. Meetings are cablecast on TS-TV Channel 58 (Comcast) and Channel 15 (WOW). Packet pages carry the MESSA Agreement (p. 87), Policyholder Resolution (p. 92), Full-Day Kindergarten (p. 93), Summer Success Academy (p. 111), Best Practices Resolution (p. 123), Facilities Study Update (p. 125), NSBA conference (p. 133) and Closed Session (p. 134).

**Recognition.** Troy High School physics teacher John Morrison and physics club students Sandeep Arakali, David Bai, Nitin Chandra, Allen Chen, Kathy Chen, Matthew Cui, Rolland He, Lawrence Kim, Maxwell Li, Richard Mu, Nikhil Ramu, Phillip Yang, Clark Zhang and Arnold Zhou won Lemelson-MIT InvenTeam status for a mechanical-assist stair climber, one of 15 high school teams nationally, receiving $10,000 for a prototype and showcasing at EurekaFest on the MIT campus, Cambridge, Massachusetts, in June.

**Minutes of November 1, 2011.** Called to order 7:00 p.m. by President Philippart, adjourned 8:48 p.m.; Edmunds, Fleming, Hauff, Malven, Miletti and Underwood present with Superintendent Fowler and administrators Birmingham, Colligan, Keeling, Machesky, Mull, Papasian, Rajter and Witt. Heather Kelly's mixed-media "Wish Project" appeared at ArtPrize 2011; AP biology teacher Rebecca Brewer was named the nation's most innovative educator in the 2011 ING Unsung Heroes Awards Program and received $27,000 for "Mini-Med School – Simulating Surgeries" for 11th and 12th grade students; the HealthierUS School Challenge Bronze Award brought each school a banner, plaque and $500, with Sodexo General Manager Gayle Moran reporting the White House invitation from First Lady Michelle Obama and 12 elementary schools recognized (Barnard, Bemis, Costello, Hamilton, Hill, Leonard, Martell, Morse, Schroeder, Troy Union, Wass, Wattles); Robert Stromayer, Director of Niles Continuing Education, was recognized for 23 years. Resolution 11-098 approved the October 4 minutes, October 18 workshop minutes, September 2011 Treasurer's Report and a spring athletic supplies bid (7-0); 11-099 approved new hire Melissa Marsack (7-0); 11-100 accepted the audited 2011 financial statements presented by Plante & Moran auditor Teresa Pollock with an unqualified opinion, thanking Mark Rajter and Monica Papasian (7-0). Ron Keoleian and Merri Lynn Colligan reported iPads bought with 2004 technology bond monies, 30 per building in two carts of 15, with Mrs. Fleming wishing for more than 660. Anne Mull reported MEAP and MME cut scores rising from 39% of answers correct to 65%, Smarter Balanced Common Core assessments in 2015 and the last MEAP in fall 2013. Student representatives Maggie Steele (Troy High) and Jonny Dowdall (Athens: first back-to-back winning seasons since 1994; OAA Red Division Football Coach of the Year Josh Heppner; varsity tennis All-Academic Team Award with a 3.93 GPA; Jennifer Wang 17th in the State Golf Finals) reported. Minutes submitted by Paula Fleming, Secretary.

**November 15, 2011 workshop.** Administration Building, 6:00 p.m. to 9:13 p.m., all seven members with Dr. Fowler, Mrs. Jagels, Mrs. Keeling, Dr. Machesky, Ms. Dixon, Mr. Hahn, Mrs. Acord and Mr. Pass; agenda covered Section 504, the Auxiliary Services Act, Special Education, Targeted Student Academic Support K-12, and Kindergarten Legislation Update/Timeline/Budget Implications.

Zinn $2,892.32 for facilities studies.

**Personnel resolutions.** Item 6.A authorizes execution of the MESSA Employer Participation Agreement for Group Welfare Benefit Programs under Section 22f(1) of the State School Aid Act, 2011 PA 62, signed by the Superintendent or her designee. Item 6.B, the Policyholder Resolution, cites MCL 388.1622f(1) and the June 1, 2012 deadline, notes coverage through MESSA and, as of January 1, 2012, Blue Cross Blue Shield, ADN, National Vision Administrators and Reliance Standard, and names Troy School District the policyholder of all such policies, including MESSA branded plans.

**Full-Day Kindergarten.** Memorandum of December 1, 2011 from Jan Keeling to Dr. Barbara Fowler, Assistant Superintendent, Elementary Instruction, 4400 Livernois, 248/823-4000, responding to pending legislation changing state kindergarten funding and weighing full-day kindergarten for 2012-2013 against potentially losing half of the foundation allowance per kindergartner. Dr. Joan Lessen-Firestone, Director of Early Childhood at Oakland Schools, presented "Full-Day Kindergarten: Why Does it Matter?", reporting gains in achievement, literacy and language (notably for ELL students, lasting through at least middle school), conduct and individualization, with Common Core fully implemented in most states by 2014-2015. The draft timeline runs from communications pieces and a district kindergarten committee in January 2012 through Schools of Choice advertising February 1, a Joan Firestone parent presentation February 15, Round-Up mailings February 22, assignment of Somerset kindergartners to Bemis, Morse or Schroeder March 15, Round-Ups March 21–29, the Schools of Choice lottery April 10, enrollment projections and new teacher postings in late April, notification letters April 27–May 1, SOC registration May 7–18, materials orders May 21–June 1, and August 2012 in-service.

**Summer Success Academy.** Reported by Dr. Richard Machesky, Assistant Superintendent for Secondary Instruction, the district's first program of its kind served 49 students entering 9th grade in 2011-2012 from Baker, Boulan Park, Larson and Smith middle schools; 81 were invited and 53 signed commitment forms. It ran 24 sessions, seven more than normal summer school, 8:30 a.m. to 1:30 p.m., with two 90-minute blocks of English and Algebra 1, a 50-minute study skills class, transportation and meals and up to 1.0 elective credit, at NCHS with instructors Anne Costello and Drew LaTorre; benchmarks cited were ACT Reading 21 and ACT Math 22. First-quarter report cards showed Athens with 26 participants at an average SSA GPA of 2.20 against 1.91 for non-SSA students and average E's of 1.18 against 1.67, and Troy with 23 participants at 2.57 against 2.53.

**Best Practices Incentive.** Section 22f provides $100 per pupil one-time grants to districts satisfying at least four of five criteria not later than June 1, 2012 (MCL 388.1622f). The district certifies it is the designated policyholder for medical benefit plans (22f(1)(b)); will continue a Service Consolidation Plan (22f(1)(c)), a signed resolution having gone to the Michigan Department of Education on September 13, 2011 with status reports due by February 1 each year; has obtained competitive bids on non-instructional services (22f(1)(d)); and will link the MI School Data Portal dashboard indicators from the district home page (22f(1)(e)). The resolution is filed with the State Aid and School Finance Office.

**Facilities Study and other items.** Co-chairs Greg Bryen and Waqar Hashim reported for the 18-member Facilities Study Team, with recommendations due at the February 7, 2012 meeting; the charge includes equity among schools, maintaining K-5, 6-8 and 9-12 grade configurations and the IB K-12 program, and excludes vacant properties monitored for sale as well as staffing, program assignment and class size. Step 1 (organize, October) is complete and Step 2 (information gathering, November) is in process with elementary building tours and two task teams. Under Board Policy B-2001, Workshops and Conferences, the Board considers Board President Philippart attending the National School Boards Association Annual Federal Relations Network Conference in Washington, D.C., February 5–7, 2012, Troy Schools being one of six districts selected by the Oakland County School Board Association for a $500 scholarship. The meeting closes with a closed session on negotiations under the Michigan Open Meetings Act, Public Act 267, Section 8(c).
